_comment: A market map of the robotics, robot-model and robot-data space, written by hand. The derived watch lists can only find publishers already in the index, which is why they missed TheRobotStudio (SO-ARM100, the arm behind 64 of our datasets), unitreerobotics (unitree_sdk2) and Pantheon (Argus, published two days before a harvest). This list exists to be independent of what we have already seen.
_scope: Includes companies that build no hardware at all: foundation-model labs, data-tooling companies, simulation vendors and big-tech research groups. A company earns a place by mattering to the field, not by selling a robot. Several have no public repositories or datasets — that is recorded as a fact about what is findable, not a judgement about the company.
_handles: github and huggingface are account handles. verified:true means the handle has been confirmed to exist; verified:false means it is a best guess. A wrong handle costs one wasted API call and returns nothing, so the cost of guessing is far lower than the cost of omitting. Anything marked false should be confirmed before the list is relied on.

_fields: founded is a stated year, looked up or known, never guessed. first_published is the year of the earliest repository seen from that account: measured, accurate for recent companies, useless for old ones — KUKA's first repository is 116 years after the company started. stage is recent (2020 or later), established (before 2020), uncertain where the only evidence is an old first repository on an unverified handle, unknown where there is no evidence at all, and n/a for labs and projects. stage_source says which of those applied.
